title: `convert_v2_to_sdk_format` returns an empty list for a list of operand dicts, so a policy rule can be created or updated with none of the conditions the caller supplied.

blocks.heading: `convert_v2_to_sdk_format` returns an empty list for a list of operand dicts, so a policy rule can be created or updated with none of the conditions the caller supplied.

blocks.text: The function's docstring says it *"never drops entries"*. It does, silently, for one input shape.
The dict branch is entered when every element is a `dict`, but it only ever reads `cond.get("operands", [])`:

blocks.code:
if isinstance(conditions, list) and all(isinstance(x, dict) for x in conditions):
    converted = []
    for cond in conditions:
        operator = cond.get("operator", "OR").upper()
        operands = cond.get("operands", [])      # <-- flat operand dicts have no "operands" key
        for operand in operands:                 # <-- loop never runs
            ...
    return converted                             # <-- []

blocks.text: So a caller passing operand dicts *without* an `{"operator", "operands"}` wrapper gets `[]` back with no error. The tuple branch above is skipped (the elements are dicts, not lists/tuples), and the terminal `raise ValueError("Unsupported conditions format: ...")` is never reached because the `all(isinstance(x, dict))` branch already matched and returned.

blocks.code:
from zscaler_mcp.common.zpa_helpers import convert_v2_to_sdk_format

flat = [
    {"object_type": "app",        "values": ["<id>"]},
    {"object_type": "scim_group", "values": [["idp-1", "group-a"]]},
]
print(convert_v2_to_sdk_format(flat))

blocks.text: Expected: either the converted conditions, or a `ValueError` naming the accepted shapes.
No credentials or network access needed — this is pure input conversion.

`[]` is not distinguishable downstream from "the caller supplied no conditions". A policy-rule create or update that receives it therefore proceeds with an empty condition set, so a rule intended to be scoped to an application and a group is written with no criteria at all, and the call reports success. On an `ALLOW` rule that is the difference between "this group, this app" and "everything the policy set covers".

The shape is an easy one to arrive at: it is what you get by taking the `conditions` structure back out of a `get`/list response and passing it to an update, and it mirrors the flattened operand shape used elsewhere in the codebase.
Two independent changes, either of which removes the silent failure:

blocks.item: Accept the flat shape — treat a dict carrying `object_type`/`objectType` at the top level as a

blocks.text: single-operand condition, so one code path handles both shapes.

blocks.item: Never return empty for non-empty input — if `conditions` was non-empty and the result is

blocks.text: empty, raise, quoting the accepted shapes. This also covers the `if not obj_type: continue` and missing-`lhs`/`rhs` paths, which drop individual operands the same way.
Happy to open a PR for either or both if useful.
